hypotheses.mechanism: Swaps (1,528 FN, oracle +0.032) are not linker errors. I measured this on the exp39+ef graph (scratch scripts claude_ls_swapedge.py and claude_ls_mid.py; the numbers are in the .notes.md file). The competitor edges out of p_u and into p_v are ordinary smooth steps: median length 1.43 / 1.41 um (TP edges 1.39), median prob 0.77 / 0.75, and 1,457 / 1,508 of them are FP. At frame t the GT node u sits 4.31 um from its nearest prediction (2nd nearest 6.38). The two competitor tracks A_t and B_t are 9.39 um apart, and u lies 2.97 um from their midpoint. Our nuclei spacing (pred-pred nearest neighbour) has median 8.71 um. So u sits in a HOLE, half a nucleus spacing from anything we detected. That is a missed nucleus between two tracked neighbours. The optimal 7 um matcher assigns u to A and v to B, which turns one missed track into 1 FN + 2 FP per frame. The same family: 2,390 GT nodes are unmatched with nearest prediction 8.42 um (a full gap; they feed a_never = 1,907 FN), and 13,050 matched GT nodes (10%) have nearest prediction > 3.5 um. So the 0.983 'annotated node recall' is inflated by 7 um matching to neighbours. Nodes are cheap in this metric: +1% nodes = -0.00092, while one recovered swap = +2.06e-5. A real missed nucleus is therefore worth ~40x its node cost at the 3.2% annotation rate. Uniform threshold lowering stayed flat (A3) because it also adds duplicates next to existing nodes, and those steal matches. A learned, hole-restricted admission avoids that failure mode by construction.
hypotheses.change: Candidates: sub-threshold peaks from a full-frame public-primary pass at 0.90. This is B35 step A's peak cache (tools/recover_daughters.py), which already reached 151/151 daughters at +24% candidate nodes. Keep only peaks >= 4.0 um from every node of the final tail graph (hole criterion; this removes duplicates, since NMS is 3 um). Features per candidate: peak score (primary/secondary/TTA agreement if cached), distances to the 1st/2nd kept node, distance to the midpoint of the two nearest kept nodes, the 1st-neighbour distance relative to the frame median spacing, local density n10, z depth, and CHAIN persistence (number of consecutive frames with a hole candidate within 3 um of the previous one, forward and backward), plus peak scores at t-1/t+1 along the chain. Model: HistGBM, 5 leak-group folds from splits.json plus a cross-embryo fit. Label: within 3 um of any GT node (positive-unlabelled; the base rate for real nuclei is the 3.2% matched rate of kept nodes, so precision = matched rate / 0.032). Insertion after the tail, before linefit: admit chains with >= 3 frames and p above tau, link along the chain (Hungarian <= 4 um), no links into existing tracks, cap added nodes at 2-3% per video. Ship: a GBM dump (a few hundred KB) plus about 150 lines in the post-processing cell. The peak pass costs about one extra detector pass (it could reuse the TTA heatmaps already computed at 0.965 by thresholding at 0.90).
hypotheses.upper_bound: Swaps: 1,528 x (7.4e-6 FN->TP + 2 x 6.6e-6 FP removed) = +0.0315. a_never: 1,907 x 7.4e-6 = +0.014. Ceiling ~+0.046 local, before node cost. Node cost: +2% nodes = -0.0018 (4.13M pred nodes -> 83k added). If 20% of the hole FN are recovered: +0.009 - 0.0018 = ~+0.007 local. At 10%: +0.0028.
hypotheses.lab_test: Step 0 (reach audit, CPU, 1 h): with friend A's 0.90 peak cache (or a new Kaggle GPU pass of recover_daughters.py over 199 videos, ~2 GPU h), count the swap/a_never GT nodes (fn_exp39_ef.parquet) that have a hole-candidate peak within 2.5 um. Kill if reach < 30% at <= 3% added candidates. Step 1: fit the OOF GBM. Report the matched rate of admitted candidates per embryo; it must exceed 2x the 3.2% base on both embryos, cross-embryo. Step 2: insert via a replay.py config key (ins-holes) on SELECTION (64 6bba), then one CONFIRMATION run. Gate: >= +0.002 overall, each embryo >= +0.001, node ratio <= +3%, gains on >= 55% of videos per embryo. Success number: +0.004 on confirmation. Honesty check: rebuild the 44b6 candidates with friend A's 6bba-only primary (never saw 44b6) and require >= half the gain on 44b6.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.002..+0.008 (10-25% of the 0.046 ceiling minus 0.0015-0.0028 node cost). Public +0.001..+0.006: the test detector is out-of-sample, so it probably misses more nuclei (more headroom), but sub-threshold evidence is noisier.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: HIGH-MEDIUM. (1) The public detector trained on these GT nuclei, so train-set sub-threshold peaks at annotated holes may be over- or under-represented relative to the test. Use the 6bba-only primary check. (2) Node-multiplier artefact (forum: min-track-length +0.013 offline / -0.004 public): here nodes are ADDED, so the multiplier works against us locally too and cannot fake a gain. (3) Corner annotations can mimic holes (GT between two nuclei with no nucleus there). The chain persistence plus a peak-score requirement filters those, because corners have no peak.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Readmit (x138/thtennant) only re-adds >= 0.965 peaks within 4 um of an OPEN track end/start. Gapfill bridges end->start gaps, and threshold lowering (A3, A29) admits all peaks uniformly, duplicates included. The swap geometry has NO open end: both competitor tracks are continuous, smooth, 1.4 um steps. So no end/start method can reach it. B25 was learned PRUNING, closed because pruned nodes sat inside tracks. This is learned ADMISSION restricted to holes >= 4 um from any kept node, a different sign and a different population. Detector fine-tunes are not involved: frozen public weights, only a lower read-out threshold plus a CPU classifier.

hypotheses.mechanism: 624 FN (10.2% of the 6,099 after ef) are a_tail: the prediction existed in the ckpt graph and the tail (short-track filter / isolated prune / leaf prune) removed it (u_reason 'tail' 482, v_reason 'tail' 450). Hand length rules transfer badly (min len 4: -0.002 LB; 8: -0.001; forum stricter length +0.013 offline / -0.004 public). The reason is that length is a poor proxy: a short component can be (a) a duplicate or fragment next to a kept track, which steals matches, or (b) a real nucleus in a hole, which carries annotated edges at the 3.2% base rate and costs only 1/350 of a TP edge per node. My hole geometry (unmatched GT nodes sit 8.4 um from any kept node; pred spacing 8.7 um) gives a feature that separates (a) from (b): distance and midpoint-ness relative to the nearest kept nodes. Length cannot see this.
hypotheses.change: For every component or node the tail removes, score it with an OOF classifier (HistGBM, leak-group folds, cross-embryo check). Features: component length, min/mean edge prob, removal stage, distance to the nearest kept node (median over the component's frames), midpoint-ness between the two nearest kept nodes, the fraction of frames where it is >= 4 um from any kept node, whether a kept track has an end/start within 4 um and 1-2 frames (fragment continuation), and density n10. Label: the component's official d_TP/d_FP if kept, computed exactly in the lab by rescoring with and without it. The target is the net edge delta, not 'annotated'. Keep components with predicted net gain > node cost (length x 2.1e-8). No new nodes beyond what the ckpt already had. Pure post-processing, <100 lines, GBM file shipped in the notebook.
hypotheses.upper_bound: 624 FN x 7.4e-6 = +0.0046 if every removed-but-true node came back with no extra FP. Node cost of keeping all removed short components is unknown (it is measurable in the lab). Min len 4 on the LB (-0.002) says 'keep all' is net negative, so the achievable part is the selective share: a realistic 30-50% of 0.0046 = +0.0014..+0.0023, minus < 0.0005 node cost.
hypotheses.lab_test: CPU only (Kaggle CPU kernel via tools/kaggle_lab.py): friend A's cache has ckpt graphs, so replay the tail with a keep-hook. Build per-component labels on SELECTION, fit leak-group OOF, apply at 3 thresholds, pick one on SELECTION, run CONFIRMATION once. Gate: >= +0.002 overall, each embryo >= +0.001, node ratio <= +0.5%, >= 55% of videos per embryo. Success number: +0.0015 confirmation with 44b6 >= +0.001 (44b6 has only 86 a_tail FN, so the per-embryo gate will be the binding constraint).
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.0005..+0.002 local; about the same on public if the per-embryo gate holds (post-proc on existing nodes transferred when the gate held, e.g. leaf prune +0.0006 local vs LB tie).
hypotheses.transfer_risk: MEDIUM. The main risk is that the component's edge probabilities are in-sample (the edge network trained on the 199 videos). Mitigation: fit a second model without edge-prob features, and ship it if it is within 80% of the full model. The node multiplier is controlled because the model optimises exact official deltas that include the node term.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: A19/A21 were hand min-length changes and B25 learned pruning of all raw peaks. Both closed. Here only the tail's own removals get a learned second opinion, with a hole feature that length lacks, and labels are exact official deltas instead of 'annotated vs not'. Leaf prune (L4) is the opposite direction (removing) and stays.

hypotheses.mechanism: Linefit (per-node linear fit over +-2 frames, weight 0.8, isotropic in voxel space) is the largest post-processing stage (+0.0145). It is a unimodal hand optimum (B28), yet it still moves 353 ckpt nodes by more than 7 um (a_linefit FN, 5.8%). Coordinates matter for this metric. FP edges have their far endpoint matched at median 4.1 um versus 1.7-2.0 um for TP edges (31% vs 10-12% beyond 3.5 um), and float output alone was +0.0024 on 70 videos (another agent's zs70.log). I tested the obvious learned version, a GBM predicting the full 3-D offset GT - pred from track context (130,928 matched nodes). Leak-group 5-fold, 6bba: mean |d| 1.963 -> 1.683 um, > 3.5 um 10.2% -> 7.7%. But cross-embryo, 44b6 gets WORSE (1.731 -> 1.849): the offset vector learns the embryo-specific annotation bias (6bba mean dz -0.85 um, 44b6 -0.16), matching the forum's -0.0031 for a constant shift. The fix is to learn only a bias-free quantity: a per-node, per-axis SCALAR weight w in [0,1] between the (sub-voxel, x138-refined) detector coordinate and the linear fit. A convex blend of two of our own estimates cannot learn a translation, so it cannot overfit an embryo's annotation bias. It can still learn WHEN smoothing hurts: turns, crowded neighbours, jumps, synthetic gap nodes, and near-fork nodes.
hypotheses.change: After the x138 port (float coordinates end to end), replace the fixed weight 0.8 with w_axis = sigmoid(f(features)). Features: fit residual per axis, turn cos, step lengths in/out, cv residual, edge probs in/out, density n10, nearest-neighbour distance, synthetic/gap flags, head shift magnitude, and window length available. Train f OOF (HistGBM or ridge on logit targets) to minimise |GT - blended| on matched nodes. The closed form per node gives the optimal w clipped to [0,1] as the regression target. Use leak-group folds and select by the CROSS-EMBRYO distance reduction. Optionally extend the window to +-3 with learned per-lag weights (still convex). Output unrounded if the x138 port confirms floats are accepted, else round last.
hypotheses.upper_bound: a_linefit 353 FN x 7.4e-6 = +0.0026, plus the general matching gain. Float output alone gave +0.0024, which is about the sensitivity of the score to ~0.3-0.5 um of coordinate error. A learned weight that recovers half the 6bba in-fold distance gain (-7% mean |d|) without the bias term is worth roughly another +0.001..+0.002. Ceiling ~+0.004.
hypotheses.lab_test: CPU (Kaggle CPU kernel): coordinates only, so topology is fixed and rescoring with the official scorer is exact (the zshift_eval.py-style harness: rewrite tail coords, score_geffs per video). Inputs are friend A's ckpt coords (pre-linefit) plus the V1284 capture once the port lands. Readouts per embryo: mean |d|, share > 3.5 um, edge TP/FP, score. Select on SELECTION; one CONFIRMATION run; gate >= +0.002, both embryos >= +0.001. Kill criterion: cross-embryo 44b6 mean |d| must fall (the full-offset model failed exactly here).
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.003 local on top of the x138 port; public similar, since nothing learned is embryo-specific.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: LOW-MEDIUM. Convex weights cannot import annotation bias. The residual risk is that the x138 head already captures most of the gain, so the increment on top of the port may be < 0.001. Measure it only after the port's own lab readout.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B28 swept only the global (weight, window) of the hand rule (unimodal optimum at 0.8/2). The x138 port is a per-frame image head with no temporal context. Constant offsets are refuted (forum -0.0031, and my cross-embryo test). This is a per-node learned smoothing weight on top of sub-voxel coordinates, a mechanism nobody has run. It is explicitly bias-free by construction, and my measurement shows why that is necessary.

hypotheses.mechanism: Two defects share one fix. (1) The lab is in-sample for every stage that trusts the edge network, which trained on all 199 videos. Relink-off won locally and lost 0.002 on the LB, and ef's +0.016 rests on ILP agreement from the same network. (2) Relink costs use learned_edge_probs built ONLY from the ILP SOLUTION edges, so every non-ILP pair gets prob 0 even though the transformer scored the whole kNN candidate graph. After ef, those zero-prob pairs still matter: u_diverted FN have p_v's in-edge at prob 0 (116 TP / 73 FP), and 'unscored & ILP both none' holds 33.5k edges (341 TP / 268 FP evaluable). My measurements also show that post-hoc DROP re-scorers on our parquet features are dead: residual FP-vs-TP cross-embryo AUC 0.853 is the same as edge_prob alone (0.852), and the best drop saves only 84 FP for 55 TP (+0.0002). On the unscored set, a GBM (AUC 0.81) never beats the ef rule. So the remaining learnable signal must come from the network's own pair scores, available for ALL candidate pairs and made honest out of fold.
hypotheses.change: On Kaggle GPU: one capture pass over 199 videos (the same pass as the V1284 capture) dumps per-node UNet features plus the kNN candidate graph. Train SimpleNodeTransformer in 5 leak-group folds (splits.json) from the public init, 5 x ~30 min. Output OOF probabilities for every candidate pair. In the pipeline: (a) pass the full candidate-graph probabilities into motion_relink_edges (bonus x prob for all scored pairs, prob 0 only for pairs outside the kNN graph); (b) re-select ef / leaf-prune / DaughterNet-insertion thresholds with OOF probabilities in the lab. At inference the shipped model is the public network (or the fold-average), so only the probability plumbing changes in the notebook.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Direct: the residual unscored-related errors are ~450 TP / ~340 FP evaluable (u_diverted zero-prob in-edges + ILP-both-none). Fixing half gives about (225 x 7.4e-6 + 170 x 6.6e-6) = +0.0028. The indirect value is avoiding one wrong adoption like relink-off (-0.002) among the ~6 remaining probes.
hypotheses.lab_test: Step 1 (inflation audit, success number): compare in-sample vs OOF edge-prob AUC on evaluable candidate pairs per embryo. If OOF AUC is within 0.01, the lab is trustworthy and the retrain stops there (saves GPU). Step 2: rerun exp48 + ef on SELECTION with OOF probabilities and with full-candidate relink probabilities, then one CONFIRMATION run. Gate: >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001. Also report the ef delta under OOF probabilities: if it shrinks by more than 50%, flag probe 29 as in-sample.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Direct +0.000..+0.003 local, public similar. Its main value is protecting the next ~6 probe decisions (one avoided -0.002 mis-adoption = +0.002).
hypotheses.transfer_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH on feasibility: the giorgosin trainer was judged not LOEO-ready (B34: Kaggle-only paths, fixed validation pair, no resume). Adapting it to folds is about 1 day, and the GPU capture shares the V1284 capture budget. Transfer of the probability plumbing itself is low risk because it only changes relink costs for pairs the network already scores at test time.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B34 was an appearance-aware linker (a new architecture) dropped for GPU priorities. This is the SAME network retrained by leak-group folds for honest probabilities, plus a plumbing fix (full-candidate probs to relink) that no relink-knob probe touched: bonus 2.5 (probe 22) scaled prob 0 for all non-ILP pairs, so it could not change them. Relink knobs, gshift and mutual-best are cost-shape changes, not probability-coverage changes.
